# Vision development — the PROTOCOL

*Binding on every rung. Distilled from ten pre-registrations, nine of which failed, and
three "earned" results that had to be retracted. Every rule below exists because
violating it cost real work. Read before writing any code.*

## 0. The paradigm-forcing rule

**The adapter supplies UNSTRUCTURED entropy and a clock. The GRAPH makes the
STRUCTURE.** Any rule that decides something is a seed rule; Python only translates
I/O and advances time. Every ablation is expressed as **graph DATA** (a flag on a
params node), never as a Python code path — so the ablation is the agent's own
configuration, not a fork in the host.

If you hand the agent a structure it was supposed to grow, you have bolted vision on.
That is what `vision_corpus.preprocess_patches` did (a hand-built retina) and what
Stage 1's six `designed:1.0` kernels did.

## 1. Gate the MEASURE before the agent

**A gate whose measure passes noise is not a gate.** Before asserting any structure:

- run the measure on **random input** — it must score at the floor;
- run it on an **ideal exemplar** of the structure — it must score high;
- run it against **learning duration** — if the score changes with how long you trained
  on the *same* input **while duration is NOT your independent variable**, you are
  reading an arbitrary point on a drift curve and every arm comparison is meaningless.
  (See §1.2 — this clause was mis-stated until Troxler, and read literally it forbade
  the phenomenon it was meant to protect.)
- **the fourth clause, earned by rung 8B: the ARMS MUST BE ALIVE. "Scores at the
  floor" is SATISFIED BY DEATH.**
- **the fifth clause, earned by FM-0 (§13.2): the MECHANISM MUST MOVE SOMETHING
  DOWNSTREAM.** Toggle it; measure `max|on − off|` on every attribute you claim it
  affects. `D == 0.0` exactly ⇒ decorative ⇒ STOP, burn no seed. **"Works" and
  "is load-bearing" are different properties.**

Stage 1's sign classifiers passed random noise 50–75% of the time AND failed an ideal
Gabor. Anisotropy passed the first two checks and failed the third for nine attempts.
**Calibrate on all five.**

### §1.2 A DURATION-CONFOUNDED MEASURE ≠ A DURATION-DEPENDENT PHENOMENON (Troxler, 2026-07-17)

**Clause 3 as originally written forbade Troxler**, which IS a change in score with
duration on the same input — that is the *phenomenon*, not a confound. The Troxler agent
hit this and needed the clause's honest form. **The discriminator is whether DURATION IS
YOUR INDEPENDENT VARIABLE, and whether every arm spans it identically:**

- **CONFOUND (what clause 3 was built to catch):** arms compared at a *single timepoint*
  on a curve that is still moving. Which arm "wins" then depends on when you looked —
  which is exactly how nine anisotropy attempts died, and why §2 (does the rule converge
  on its own input?) exists at all.
- **PHENOMENON (Troxler):** duration is the axis; **all arms run the same 3200 steps**;
  the contrast is between two *time-courses*, not between two points. Drift 0.134050 vs
  stabilised 0.000227, paired, 8/8, p=0.007812.

**The original catch is preserved and nothing is weakened:** if you are reporting a single
number per arm and that number drifts with duration, clause 3 still kills you. **The
exemption is narrow — you must declare duration as the IV in advance, and every arm must
span it identically.** A post-hoc "duration was my variable all along" is forking paths
(§4) wearing this clause as a costume.

### §1.1 A DEAD ARM SCORES A PERFECT FLOOR (rung 8B, 2026-07-17)

`complex_cells.osi()` ends `return (a-b)/(a+b) if (a+b) > 1e-9 else 0.0`. **So a cell
that never fires returns 0.0000 — a flawless floor — and is indistinguishable from a
cell that fires everywhere equally.** Rung 8B's GCAL-θ arm passed **every** one of its
four pre-registered criteria (ideal 1.0000, floor 0.0000, separation 1.0000 on BOTH
pathways) while its floor arm **fired at 0 of 12 orientations**. The "separation" was
measuring **fires vs does-not-fire**. A trained cell that failed to develop would have
scored 0.0000 and one that developed 1.0000 — H1 would have been a coin flip dressed as
a result.

**§12's rule generalises to instruments of this shape: an absence off a GUARDED DIVISION
(`if denom > eps else 0.0`) is evidence of a LOOKUP, not of a measurement** — the same
disease as `.get('Name','')`, in float form. **Positive-control the ARM, not only the
reader:** report how many of the probe's conditions the cell responds to at all, and
treat a silent arm as a failed gate, never as a good floor. (Rung 8B's own `G0` reader
was in turn positive-controlled: it returns 12/12 on a responsive arm and 0/12 on the
dead one.)

**Corollary — `peak/base` is an UNBOUNDED ratio and has now blown up in TWO independent
rungs.** The calibration reframe died on it (`base`→0 ⇒ the no-input control scored
**1.6×10⁶** vs an ideal Gabor's 6.94; ledger 10000–10999); rung 8B read **7.1×10⁷** and
**2.4×10⁸** from the same cause. It should be bounded or retired, not read.

**And the direction matters (§5).** Rung 8B declared its own PASS invalid. That is not
metric surgery: §5 forbids changing a measure to **rescue** a failure. Making a measure
**stricter against yourself** is always allowed, and is what §1 and §7 demand.

A gate that checks a rule's CONSTANTS but not the AXIS they parameterise is not a gate
(the "~1s window" was gated by its constants while being one step wide).

## 2. The rule must CONVERGE on its own input distribution

**Before any experience/ablation arm is run, measure: does the rule settle?**
Checkpoint anisotropy AND drift (‖w(t)−w(t−Δ)‖/‖w‖) out to ≥3200 steps on the
formative input alone.

- **CONVERGENT + USEFUL:** score plateaus at non-zero structure AND drift → 0.
- **Never converges** (fixed-sign Butts: drift 0.49–0.75, decayed *through* the random
  floor) ⇒ the scaffold is a TRANSIENT and every arm is measured at an arbitrary point
  on a decay curve.
- **Converges to death** (BCM: drift → 0 at 0.004 structure) ⇒ equally useless.

**This single check explains nine failed attempts. Run it FIRST.** A rule with no
stable fixed point cannot model development, where prolonged exposure to formative
statistics stabilises a representation.

### §2.1 "CONVERGED" AND "TERMINATED" ARE DIFFERENT PROPERTIES — and the engine only has the second (2026-07-17, the non-bipartite sheet)

**A settled sheet DITHERS AT ONE ULP, FOREVER, and `run_rules` calls every tick of
it progress.** Measured tick-by-tick (`VISION_SETTLE8_RESULTS.md` §3.4): `st_settle`
writes an `act_next` **one ULP** from `act`; `st_commit` copies it back; repeat —
**200,000 applications per step on a sheet whose dynamics reached a fixed point to
1e−16.** At c=4: **4.0 ULP**. At c=8: **1.0 ULP**. **Neither is a dynamics.**

**`run_rules` terminates on EXACT VALUE EQUALITY. "Settled" is a TOLERANCE
predicate. A contraction's fixed point is generically NOT exactly representable in
float64**, so the iteration lands in a period-2 orbit between the two nearest
floats and never satisfies exact equality. **This is not a fact about a lattice, a
seed, or a spectrum — it is a fact about exact-equality fixpoints over float
arithmetic, and it afflicts any relaxation this substrate ever runs.**

**THE RULES:**

1. **Never infer "it did not converge" from "it did not terminate."** Measure the
   **AMPLITUDE** of what it lands on. `~1e-16` ⇒ **CONVERGED, and the engine cannot
   see it**. `O(1)` ⇒ a genuine orbit. **The settling rung read 200000/200000 and
   concluded "no fixed point exists"; the sheet had settled.**
2. **An exact-equality test is a LOOKUP, not a measurement of dynamics** — §1.1's
   guarded-division disease in a new costume. `array_equal` returns "not a fixed
   point" for a sheet at 1e−16. **Amplitude is the discriminator; the equality test
   is a proxy.**
3. **A residual read off a SINGLE SNAPSHOT is PHASE-DEPENDENT and will lie to you.**
   `|act − act_next|` is **exactly 0.0** on the post-commit phase and **1 ULP** on
   the post-settle phase of the *same* dithering orbit. **Sampling it once on a
   period-2 orbit is a coin flip** — it read `0.000e+00` on a sheet burning the cap
   forever. **Tick one at a time and watch, or do not claim.**
4. **THE SPECTRUM IS NOT THE RECTIFIED LOOP.** `ρ(M) < 1` is a claim about the
   LINEARISATION. The loop is `max(aff + M·act, 0)` and **the ReLU is not `M`** —
   it clamps units, and **the active set, not the lattice, is what the dynamics
   actually run on**. Measured: the bipartite lattice's λ_min=−1 checkerboard
   survives the ReLU on **0.000–0.005** of realistic (sparse) drives, because **the
   checkerboard needs the WHOLE lattice and a lattice with holes is not bipartite**.
   **A linear-algebra theorem generalised to a rectified loop without measuring the
   rectified loop is not a theorem about your system.**

**And the §13 pay-off, because this is where a constant would normally sneak in:**
the fix is **NOT** to import GCAL's 16. **GCAL's 16 IS a tolerance predicate wearing
a count's clothes** — its own paper says the number is *"sufficient to ensure that
cortical activity is no longer changing significantly"* (verbatim, PMC6618482,
verified by two independent readers). The honest form of the mechanism is a fixpoint
**up to the ARITHMETIC'S OWN RESOLUTION** (`np.spacing` at the value's own scale):
**RELATIVE**, fixed by the float mantissa's noise floor rather than by the answer you
wanted, and importing **nothing** from GCAL's frame. **That is a §13 number that
falls OUT.** *(Named, NOT built — and its factor is open: the measured dithers span
**1.0–4.0 ULP**, and "tune it to 4" would be a magic number.)*

**BUILT — and NOT by that route (2026-07-18, the fixpoint predicate,
`VISION_CYCLE_DETECT_RESULTS.md`, `23000–23999` allocated/burned-none).** The
ε-route above was NOT taken, because its factor stayed open AND the degree-based
derivation of it was **refuted by re-measuring the dither** (c=4 → 4.0 ULP, c=8 →
1.0 ULP: more degree, LESS dither, because ρ<1 damps round-off and ρ is not
something a rule can know). Instead: **a period-2 ULP dither IS a fixed point of
the 2-step map**, and rule application is a DETERMINISTIC map, so a **repeated
graph state** proves the trajectory is periodic. Termination becomes "have I been
in this exact state before" — exact equality against HISTORY, **NO TOLERANCE, NO
ε, NO CONSTANT AT ALL** (the strongest §13 outcome: not a number that falls out,
but *no number*). `TypedGraph::state_fingerprint()` + an opt-in `detect_cycles` on
`run_rules`, **OFF by default** (§9: byte-identity proven across two binaries;
bench 200/0; every committed contract unmoved). It returns the **bit-identical**
settled sheet the cap would (`max|act_off−act_on| = 0.0` exactly), 30 000–50 000×
cheaper. **It fixes TERMINATION, not the ceiling:** ρ(M)→1 as the sheet grows is
untouched, and an exploratory pilot finds the default η near-vacuous on the settled
sheet — **8D's convergent-AND-load-bearing η is still unfound**, now with the
mechanism to hunt it at scale (the `wave_world.step` opt-in is REPORTED, not made,
§11.4).

## 3. Pre-registration — mandatory, written and COMMITTED before the run

Every claim needs a file section written *before* looking, containing:

1. **Hypothesis**, two-sided (predicted directions in this arc were wrong four times).
2. **The statistic**, exactly.
3. **n, FIXED IN ADVANCE** by a power analysis on a pilot restricted to
   **already-burned** seeds.
4. **Confirmatory seeds never used for anything** (keep a burned-seed ledger).
5. **Decision rule**, including what a null means.
6. **Exactly the listed tests. No sweeps. No re-runs.** A further attempt needs a NEW
   pre-registration with a NEW mechanism-level hypothesis — never a parameter search.
7. **Your prediction, stated in advance**, with its provisos. (Being right in advance is
   the only evidence you understand the model; a proviso that breaks tells you what you
   didn't understand.)

## 4. Analysis rules that were learned the hard way

- **Unit of analysis is the SEED**, not the unit. Units in a run share input and compete
  under winner-take-all ⇒ not independent. Counting units inflated every early p-value.
- **Test the INTERACTION, not the simple effect**, whenever the no-mechanism control is
  non-null.
- **Conjunctive gates** where a mechanism could pass by making itself inert
  (`d_a > 0` AND `d_b < 0`). Attempt 2 "removed the harm" by removing the effect.
- **Adding a mechanism can silently invalidate your control.** Re-derive what each arm
  MEANS after every change (`unit_burst_steps=3` made "window=0" no longer the
  no-mechanism condition).
- **Replicate on fresh seeds before believing.** p=0.013 and p=0.0016 both evaporated.
- **~15 comparisons reported selectively is a forking-paths garden**, even while quoting
  the rule against it.

## 5. Never rescue a failed gate by changing the measure

Metric surgery. If a failure suggests the readout is wrong, that is a **new hypothesis
requiring its own prospective pre-registration** — never a reinterpretation of the data
that just failed. (The refinement hypothesis was tested prospectively and failed:
+0.042, p=0.15. That is how it is done.)

## 6. Controls must correspond to the actual experiment

`dark` was set to "no input" for two pre-registrations. **Dark-reared animals keep their
waves** — that is *why* they have maps, and `VISION_RUNG1_PLAN.md` said so in those
words before the error was made. Pre-registration protects the statistics; **it does not
protect the design.** Before running, state what each arm corresponds to *in the animal*
and check it against the research.

Robustness across attempts is worth nothing if the attempts share a confound: rung 1's
asymmetry survived six adversarial attempts because all six shared one design error.

## 7. Report negatives as results; retract when the evidence turns

Three "earned" results were retracted here (Stage 1's "biology emerged"; rung 1's
deprivation asymmetry; "vision refines" as an interpretation). Each retraction is
recorded in place, with the measurement that forced it. **A negative that is diagnosed
is worth more than a positive that is not understood.**

## 8. Scope discipline on every claim

State what is NOT shown. "Refined structure, not Gabors" (0.402 vs an ideal Gabor's
0.867). "No map topography measured." "This licenses nothing about which biological
mechanism is correct" (the verified research refuted the Hebbian-vs-sparsity question
0-3). Cite the research's own killed claims.

## 9. Defaults preserve committed results

Every new mechanism ships **off by default** (`bcm=0`, `oja=0`, `fovea_radius=0`) so
every committed result reproduces exactly. Verify with the migrated gates before
committing.

## 10. Every result records WHICH BINARY produced it

*A number without an engine is not a result.* On 2026-07-16 the rung-6 agent found
**two** `substrate_rs/_native.abi3.so` on this machine, and a process got whichever
`sys.path` happened to pick:

| artifact | built | status |
|---|---|---|
| `runners/dsl/python/substrate_rs/_native.abi3.so` | Jul 16 | CURRENT — byte-identical to `runners/dsl/target/release/libsubstrate_rs.so` |
| `~/.local/lib/python3.14/site-packages/substrate_rs/_native.abi3.so` | Jul 13 | **STALE** — a non-editable pip install of a Jul-3 wheel, `.so` later clobbered by a `maturin develop` build |

`conftest.py` inserts only the repo ROOT, so bare `pytest` imported the **stale**
engine while `PYTHONPATH=runners/dsl/python pytest` imported the **current** one.
**Two agents could measure two different engines and both report "green."** This one
session produced 122/0, 138/0, 145/10, 19 passed, 10/122 and 155/0 — for a suite with
ONE answer.

**The definitive side-by-side** — same commit (`a1844f2ed0`), same scope, same machine,
per-process engine isolation via `PYTHONPATH` (never mutate the shared `.pth` while
anyone is measuring):

| engine | `pytest tests/ -k vision` |
|---|---|
| fresh `95167c01b7b3` | **156 passed, 0 failed** |
| stale `ad3292c19e1f` | **11 failed, 145 passed** |

**The relayed "10 failed / 122 passed on clean HEAD" was itself a stale-binary
artifact** — it does not reproduce on the fresh engine. The stale profile is the
source of it. (The stale engine *can* collect at this commit — 156/6315, zero
collection errors — so "cannot collect the suite" does not reproduce here either.)

**The failure modes are the point, and only 4 of 11 are loud.** `ChangeDetect` raised
`UnknownTermType` ×4; the rest were SILENT:

- `vf_temporal_diff never fired` — a rule quietly not firing;
- `assert 'attention_x' in {'vision_clearance': 0.0}` ×2 — attention silently not driven;
- **`assert 36 == 9`** — a **silently WRONG NUMBER** from `test_agent_can_query_kernels_via_dsl`;
- `could not convert string to float: b'\xd1\xcc\x0c?...'` — raw bytes misread as text.

**So "bit-identical on the dorsal path" does NOT generalise to "bit-identical."** The
stale build (Jul 13 **10:55:45**) predates commit `fbf363a544` (Jul 13 **16:21**) —
*"DSL engine fix: where-clause `Eq` coerces `Str` ↔ `Surface(Text)`"* — which is
**general rule-matching semantics, not vision**. Proven on one Term tree, same inputs:

```
Eq(StringConcat("abc"), Attr(name="abc"))    fresh -> True
                                             stale -> False
```

A `where`-clause of that shape fires on one engine and not the other, **silently**.
Blast radius: **37 seeds use `StringConcat`** (composer / comprehension / conversation).
**No vision seed uses it** — which is why the dorsal path looked identical. A path that
does not exercise a divergent construct proves nothing about one that does.

**Fixed at the root (2026-07-17).** The site-packages COPY is deleted; a
`site-packages/substrate_rs.pth` points at `runners/dsl/python`, so **every** process —
any cwd, with or without `PYTHONPATH` — resolves to the ONE artifact in this tree. A
copy goes stale; a pointer cannot.

### §10.1 THAT FIX CONTRADICTED §11, AND THE CONTRADICTION WAS MINE (2026-07-17)

The `.pth` above is an **absolute path into the CANONICAL tree**. §11 then mandated that
every concurrent agent work in a **worktree**. `runners/dsl/python/substrate_rs/_native.abi3.so`
is **gitignored**, so a fresh worktree has no engine of its own and the `.pth` is the only
thing that resolves `substrate_rs` at all. Therefore:

> **Every worktree silently imported the CANONICAL tree's engine** — and, worse than
> first understood, its entire `substrate_rs` **Python package** too. The provenance gate
> **failed in every worktree** (`loaded != REPO_NATIVE`) while passing in the canonical one.

*"A copy goes stale; a pointer cannot"* was right and incomplete: **a pointer cannot go
stale, but it can point somewhere other than where you are standing.** Raised independently
by rung 7 and the Fable review — two readers, one cause, which is how you know it is the
setup and not an opinion.

**Benign so far ONLY because no rung has added Rust** (verified below, not assumed). But the
standing directive is that **engine limits are BUILD TASKS, not vetoes**, so a rung adding a
Rust Term is *expected*. On that day it would have measured the canonical binary and its own
`.rs` edit would have evaporated **silently** — reproduced: with a marker Term compiled into
a worktree's `py.rs`, `substrate_rs.version()` returned the canonical `0.1.0`, no error.

**THE ROOT FIX — the invariant is about SOURCE, not LOCATION.** The old gate asked *"does the
engine live in MY tree?"*, which is wrong twice: it is unconditionally red in every worktree
(an always-red gate is one agents route around), and it passes on a binary at the right path
built from different source. The question that protects a number is:

> **Is the loaded engine a build of THIS TREE'S Rust source?**

Sharing the canonical build across worktrees is **correct and cheap precisely when the `.rs`
is byte-identical** — the common case, since most rungs add no Rust. It is wrong the instant a
worktree touches Rust, and that is the instant the gate now fails. (Rung 7 checked this by
hand with an md5 of every `.rs`; `rust_source_fingerprint()` automates exactly that check.)

**The rules:**

1. **Record the engine on every result.** `domains/engine_provenance.py` →
   `provenance_line()` gives `engine <sha256[:12]> @ <path>` **plus the source verdict**
   (`own` / `shared` / `DIVERGED`). Paste it into every results file, log header, and
   pre-registration OUTCOME. A rung whose numbers carry no engine hash cannot be reconciled
   later — and `engine X @ path` alone does not say whether X was built from the source you
   are attributing the number to.
2. **Never install a COPY of `substrate_rs`.** No `pip install`, no plain
   `maturin develop` into site-packages — both create a second artifact that silently
   ages. Rebuild in place (`runners/dsl/`), and let resolution do its work.
3. **Resolution is TREE-RELATIVE.** `conftest.py` calls
   `engine_provenance.engine_preamble()`, which puts **this tree's** `runners/dsl/python`
   first on `sys.path`. A tree that built its own engine gets its own; a tree that may
   legitimately share one (identical Rust source) gets it **symlinked to its own path** by
   `ensure_tree_engine()`; a tree whose source diverges gets nothing and fails loudly.
   Any non-pytest entrypoint (a rung script) must call `engine_preamble()` itself.
4. **A shared build is legitimate ONLY while the Rust source is byte-identical.**
   `tests/test_engine_provenance_migrated.py` is the gate. It **passes in BOTH trees** when
   the source agrees, and **fails in BOTH** when it diverges, naming both trees, both
   fingerprints, and the build script. **If you touch `.rs` in a worktree, you MUST build
   that worktree — run `scripts/engine_build.sh`.** The gate will not let you measure
   without it. **Never hand-roll the `cp`** — see §10.3.

**§10.2 THE HEADLESS-PACKAGE TRAP — §10 rule 6 was exactly BACKWARDS in a worktree.**
`runners/dsl/python/substrate_rs/*.py` is **TRACKED**; `_native.abi3.so` is **GITIGNORED**.
So a fresh worktree ships the Python package **without its binary** — and the
`sys.path.insert(0, runners/dsl/python)` convention that rule 6 called *"safe"*, and that
*"is why no committed rung result changed"*, is precisely what **BREAKS** there: it pins a
HEADLESS package that **shadows the `.pth`** and dies with `cannot import name '_native'
... (most likely due to a circular import)` — a misleading message for a path problem.
**Measured: 3 of the 16 vision-bench files ERROR on collection in EVERY worktree**, before
any change — the same convention that pins the right engine in the canonical tree pins a
package with no engine at all in a worktree. `ensure_tree_engine()` fixes it by symlinking
a **source-identical** build to the tree's own path, so every existing preamble works
unchanged in every tree (worktree bench: 3 collection errors → **156 passed / 0 failed**).
`realpath` resolves the link, so provenance still names the REAL artifact and reads
`shared` — it never pretends the build was this tree's.

**§10.3 NEVER `cp` ONTO THE ENGINE PATH — it writes THROUGH the symlink into the CANONICAL
tree.** Because `_native.abi3.so` is now often a symlink (§10.2), the obvious build command
`cp target/release/libsubstrate_rs.so python/substrate_rs/_native.abi3.so` **follows the
link and overwrites the canonical tree's engine underneath every other agent's concurrent
run** — the exact shared-mutable-state failure §11 exists to prevent, and worse than the
bug it would be fixing. **Verified on a scratch pair: `cp new link` replaced the LINK
TARGET's contents.** Use **`scripts/engine_build.sh`**, which always uses
`cp --remove-destination` (unlink first, then copy) and re-checks provenance afterwards.
This is why the build is a script and not a `cp` in a doc: a footgun documented is a
footgun shipped.
5. **The gate is verified to fail on BOTH broken setups, in BOTH trees** — a gate that has
   never failed is not a gate, and this defect has already recurred twice in this arc:
   * **STALE** — restore the stale site-packages install ⇒ the ambiguity + capability tests
     fail.
   * **WRONG TREE** — change one byte of `.rs` in a worktree ⇒ the source-fingerprint test
     fails loudly in the worktree and passes in canonical. *Before this rewrite the same
     change was silently ignored and the canonical answer returned.*
   It checks what path discipline alone cannot: exactly ONE distinct artifact resolvable;
   the loaded engine is a build of **this tree's** source (`own` or byte-identical
   `shared`); the build is not stale w.r.t. its own `.rs`; and — the capability pin — that
   the vision Terms actually **evaluate**, which catches a stale binary at the *right* path
   with the *right* fingerprint.
6. **Scripts must not be trusted to pin it for you.** The rung scripts happened to be
   safe (`rung4_lib.py` / `rung5_measure.py` / `rung6_lib.py` each
   `sys.path.insert(0, runners/dsl/python)`, so they always loaded the repo engine —
   which is *why* no committed rung result changed). That was luck of a convention, not
   a guarantee. Tree-relative resolution + the gate make it structural.

**Audit outcome — the STALE hazard:** rungs 1/2/4/5/6 are **unaffected** — their seeds use
none of the divergent Terms (only `vision_floor.json` uses `TemporalDiff`/`Foveate`), and
their measurement scripts pinned the repo engine by preamble. The ambiguity hit the **test
bench**, not the measurements. No committed claim moves.

### 10b. §10 AND §11 CONTRADICT IN A WORKTREE — found 2026-07-17 (`W0_ABLATION.md`)

> **STATUS: DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED, AND ROOT-FIXED — see §10.1–§10.3 above, which are that
> fix.** This section is kept verbatim as the **independent corroboration**, and that is
> exactly why it is worth keeping: the w0-ablation agent, rung 7, and the Fable review each
> hit this from a different direction and diagnosed it identically, with no sight of each
> other. **Three readers, one cause** — so it is a property of the setup, not an opinion.
> Its interim advice ("copy the `.so` into your worktree, insert ahead of the `.pth`, and
> verify the PATH not merely the hash") is now **superseded**: `ensure_tree_engine()` does
> the copy-equivalent (a symlink) automatically, `engine_preamble()` does the insert, and
> the gate checks something strictly stronger than the path — **that the engine is a build
> of THIS TREE'S Rust SOURCE** (a right-path binary can still be built from wrong source;
> a shared binary from identical source is CORRECT, and forbidding it would force a
> needless cargo build on every worktree). Its second proposed root fix — *"assert the
> loaded artifact lives in the CURRENT tree"* — was **tried and rejected**: it is what the
> old test effectively did, and it fails in every worktree, making the gate unconditionally
> red. **The invariant is content, not location.**

**The `.pth` fix does NOT hold in a worktree, and §11 is what breaks it.** The
pointer installed at `site-packages/substrate_rs.pth` is an **absolute path into
the canonical tree**:

```
/home/matt/ozma/internal/research/experiments/gamma-substrate/runners/dsl/python
```

and `_native.abi3.so` is **gitignored**. So a fresh worktree (§11.1: *"one agent,
one worktree"*) has **no engine of its own** and silently resolves to **another
tree's binary** — precisely the hazard §10 exists to kill, reintroduced by §11's
isolation requirement. Worse, it is silent in the direction §10 warns about: a
worktree testing *its own* Rust change would measure the *canonical* engine and
report green.

**"A copy goes stale; a pointer cannot" is true — but a pointer to a tree you are
not in is a different failure, not a fixed one.**

**What to do, until the root fix lands:** copy the canonical release `.so` into
your worktree (a **private** copy — never a global install, §11.2), ensure your
scripts `sys.path.insert(0, <worktree>/runners/dsl/python)` ahead of the `.pth`,
and **verify with `provenance_line()` that the PATH you loaded is inside YOUR
tree** — not merely that the hash matches. The rung scripts' `sys.path.insert`
preamble already does the first half; nothing checks the second.

**Root fixes, for the supervisor to sequence (not done here — not my files):**
either make the `.pth` resolve relatively, or have
`tests/test_engine_provenance_migrated.py` assert the loaded artifact lives in
the CURRENT tree. Today it can only assert the hash, so it passes in a worktree
that is measuring someone else's binary.

**Audit outcome — the WRONG-TREE hazard (verified 2026-07-17, not assumed):**
`git diff 0a1a1ee4bb..HEAD -- runners/dsl/src runners/dsl/Cargo.toml` is **EMPTY** — the Rust
source is **byte-identical across all 51 commits of the vision arc**, from the first vision
commit to the rung-7 merge. Every rung measured in a worktree therefore got the canonical
binary *while that binary was a correct build of that worktree's own source*. The one Rust
change on this branch (`fbf363a544`, the `Eq` coercion fix) is an **ancestor** of the arc, so
it is compiled into every engine every rung used. **No committed vision result is affected**
— rung 7's assessment is confirmed independently, by content rather than by inspection.

### §10.2 THE ENGINE IS NOT THE ONLY GITIGNORED THING A WORKTREE LACKS — `data/` IS THE OTHER ONE (2026-07-17, SHAPE-SELFSEE)

§10.1 solved this for the **binary**. It has an exact twin that was still open: **`data/` is
gitignored, so a fresh worktree has no slab either** — and unlike a missing engine, a missing
slab **fails SILENTLY and PLAUSIBLY**.

Measured (`VISION_SHAPE_SELFSEE_RESULTS.md`): in a fresh worktree at `de5f96b8`,
`converse("What do you know about the moon?")` returns **`"I am Jabberwock."`** — the exact
string the committed gate asserts must be **absent** — and
`tests/test_topic_route_selfheal_migrated.py` **fails 9/13**. The agent is not broken; **its
reader is unbuilt**. Symlink `data/` → canonical: **13/13, real lunar content**. (This is the
"open-class POS cold slab" gotcha, root-caused: it is not a POS mystery, it is an absent
gitignored directory.)

**Why this is worse than a missing engine:** a missing engine throws. A missing slab returns a
**fluent, well-formed, WRONG answer** — an honest-looking floor reply. Any rung that reads the
agent's NL output in a worktree and does **not** positive-control the reader first will measure
**its own missing slab** and report it as a fact about the agent. SHAPE-SELFSEE's null would
have been **bit-identical** and **worthless** without the control.

**The rules:**

1. **Positive-control the READER before you trust one word it says.** A known-good input with a
   known-good answer (`"What do you know about the moon?"` → real lunar content, **not** `"I am
   Jabberwock."`). This is §1 clause 4 pointed at the instrument you are reading *through*.
2. **`data/` is a symlink, never a copy** (§10.1 rule 2's logic: a copy ages, a pointer cannot).
   It is gitignored, so the symlink cannot enter a commit.
3. **"The agent couldn't answer" is not a finding until the reader is proven alive.** It is the
   single cheapest way to fake a null in this project.

**AND THE §9 BASELINE IS ITSELF AN INSTANCE OF THE SKIP-GUARD DEFECT.** Measured as a paired
control (SHAPE-SELFSEE): `scripts/rung7_vision_bench.sh` gives **190 passed / 10 skipped
WITHOUT `data/`** — the recorded §9 number — and **200 passed / 0 skipped WITH it**. The 10
skips are `pytest.skip("BSDS300 corpus absent (data/vision_curriculum/BSDS300)")`
(`test_vision_curriculum_migrated.py:47`, `test_vision_growth_migrated.py:120`). Since `data/`
is gitignored and therefore absent in **every** worktree, **those 10 tests have never run in a
worktree**, while the suite reports clean green. All 10 pass when the corpus is present — which
is exactly why it went unnoticed. **The §9 baseline must be quoted WITH ITS CONDITION**
(`190/10 without data/`, `200/0 with`); a gate with 10 permanently-dormant tests is **5%
vacuous and does not know it**. *(Recorded, not actioned: §9 says defaults do not move without
review.)*

## 11. CONCURRENT AGENTS RUN IN SEPARATE WORKTREES — no shared mutable state

Multiple agents in one tree share three things they must not: **the engine, the git
index, and the seed files.** Both process failures of 2026-07-17 came from exactly that,
and neither was a mistake of judgement — they were guaranteed by the setup:

- An agent comparing engines **swapped the global `substrate_rs.pth`**, silently
  repointing the engine underneath *other agents' concurrent pytest runs*. It caught and
  discarded its own contaminated run; it could not have protected the others.
- `git add -A` **swept another agent's uncommitted edit into an unrelated commit**
  (`VISION_PROTOCOL.md` §10 → `a1844f2ed0`). Agents committing each other's half-finished
  work is the same disease as the binary hazard: *shared mutable state with no owner.*

**Rules:**
1. **One agent, one worktree.** Every concurrent agent gets its own git worktree
   (`isolation: "worktree"`), and merges when its result is committed. The supervisor
   resolves conflicts — expect them only in `domains/seed_registry.py` (registrations)
   and this file's ledger; **resolve by keeping BOTH sides**.
2. **Never mutate global install state.** Never swap/edit `site-packages/substrate_rs.pth`,
   never `pip install`/`maturin develop` into the shared env. To compare engines, use a
   **private copy + per-process `PYTHONPATH`**. The `.pth` points at the CANONICAL
   `runners/dsl/python` and must stay a pointer (§10).
   **AND: never `cp` onto `python/substrate_rs/_native.abi3.so`** — in a worktree it is
   usually a SYMLINK into the canonical tree, so a plain `cp` writes THROUGH it and
   clobbers the shared engine mid-run. Use `scripts/engine_build.sh` (§10.3).
   **This rule and §10's absolute `.pth` CONTRADICTED each other until 2026-07-17** —
   every worktree silently imported the canonical engine, and the provenance gate failed in
   every worktree while passing in the canonical one. Resolved in **§10.1–§10.3**: the
   invariant is *"the engine is a build of THIS TREE's Rust source"* (content, not
   location), resolution is tree-relative, and the gate now passes in BOTH trees when the
   source agrees and fails in BOTH when it does not. **If your rung changes Rust, run
   `scripts/engine_build.sh` — a worktree that does not is refused, not trusted.**
3. **Never `git add -A` / `git commit -a`.** Stage only the paths you own, by name. If a
   file you did not write appears in your diff, stop and report it — it is someone else's
   in-flight work.
4. **Own your files.** Do not edit another rung's seed, adapter, pre-registration or
   tests. Need a change there? Report it; the supervisor sequences it.
5. **Long-running measurement is not a lock.** Another agent may commit, merge, or rebase
   under you. Record the commit SHA *and* engine hash your numbers came from (§10), or
   they are unattributable.

A number is only as trustworthy as the isolation it was measured under. This session
produced **six different answers** (122/0, 138/0, 145/10, 19 passed, 10/122, 156/0) for a
suite that has exactly one — and the supervisor relayed two of them as fact.

## 12.3 A PROVENANCE CLAIM MUST BE PINNED TO ITS DIFF, NEVER TO A MUTABLE TREE

*Both of rung 8B's self-restraint gates ROTTED THE SAME DAY THEY WERE WRITTEN, and they
rotted by accusing an innocent rung.*

`test_this_rung_adds_NO_rust` and `test_vision_onoff_and_vision_lateral_are_NOT_edited`
each diffed the **live tree** against a **hardcoded sha** and asserted "nothing changed".
But the claim each makes is about **rung 8B's OWN COMMITS** — *rung 8B added no Rust*;
*rung 8B did not edit another rung's seed*. Tested against a mutable tree, they do not
test that claim at all: **they test whether anyone has done any work since.** The two-eyes
rung then added `PickUnique` (a legitimate, gated, §9-verified Rust Term) and rebound 25
`Pick` sites in `vision_onoff.json` — and both gates fired. **Rung 8B still added no
Rust. The gates were making a false accusation.**

**The fix is to test the INTENT, not the proxy:**
- the no-Rust gate is now pinned to **rung 8B's own commit range** (`9ca3845985^..a5ab9b859c`) — the diff its claim is actually about;
- the no-edit gate now admits **exactly** the mechanical `Pick`→`PickUnique` rebind and fails on **anything else** — because what it truly claims is that rungs 6/7 remain ATTRIBUTABLE, and that rebind is provably a no-op (`PickUnique` ≡ `Pick` at ≤1 candidate; verified two ways: bench 165/10 identical, wave floats identical to the last digit; and the diff contains 25 `-Pick` / 25 `+PickUnique` and NOTHING else).

**This is NOT metric surgery (§5).** §5 forbids changing a measure to **rescue a failure**.
Here the underlying facts were verified FIRST and independently — the diff was audited
term-by-term, and the semantics-preserving argument was checked before either gate was
touched. **Verify the fact, then fix the gate. Never the reverse.** If the diff had
contained one foreign line, the answer would have been to revert the rung, not to widen
the allowlist.

**And the fixed gate was POSITIVE-CONTROLLED** — a foreign edit was injected and the gate
went RED, then the edit was reverted and it went GREEN. **A gate you have only ever seen
pass is not a gate you have tested** (§1's fourth clause, applied to the guard rather than
the arm). **Do not widen this allowlist without the same standard: a semantics-preserving
argument, a byte-identity re-run, AND a proof the gate still bites.**

## 12.4 A SUBAGENT'S LITERATURE REVIEW IS A CLAIM, NOT A SOURCE (2026-07-17)

**A research subagent FABRICATED material mid-task.** It self-reported and retracted, and
its parent disclosed that the rest of its answers were its own less-sourced work — **but
the supervisor had already relayed all of it upstream as established.** The fabrication
was caught by the agent's own honesty, NOT by any gate.

**The standard is set by what worked the same day:** two independent agents were assigned
overlapping BCM questions; the second **retrieved the 1982 primary itself** (a different
URL from the first), read **eq. 7 off the page image**, confirmed the peer's reading,
found **Scholarpedia is wrong** (it drops the `·c̄`), and then **explicitly refused to
vouch for the peer's other claims**: *"that lies outside my assignment and I have not
verified any of it… treat them as the peer's findings, not as jointly verified."*

**RULES:**
- **A literature claim from one agent is unverified by default.** Cross-check anything
  load-bearing against a page image, by a second agent that retrieves it independently.
- **Never launder a peer's claims through your own credibility.** Report what you verified
  and what you did not, separately, and say which is which.
- **Secondary sources are not sources.** Scholarpedia was wrong about BCM's own equation;
  the "10% DVS threshold" is a convention repeated until it looked measured.
- **This applies hardest to the supervisor**, who is the relay point and the most likely to
  turn a subagent's plausible paragraph into a stated fact. It has now happened three times
  in one day (the "76 population grabs" count; the c₀-set-to-1 step; the DVS material).

## 13. MAGIC NUMBERS FALL **OUT** OF NATURAL PROCESSES — THEY DO NOT GO **IN**

*The creator's rule, 2026-07-17, minted the moment rung 8B measured `μ=0.024` killing a
cell. It is binding, and it is not a slogan: **it sorts this arc's entire ledger with no
exceptions**, which is why it is a rule and not an opinion.*

**Everything that FELL OUT stands:**

| number | fell out of |
|---|---|
| Weber–Fechner **0.9991** | a log receptor |
| Engbert **α_s 1.1553 / α_l 0.7590** (paper 0.79±0.11) | a self-avoiding walk |
| centre-surround **CS 1.0839** | rung 7's decorrelation — **from a ZERO init** |
| **σ_ON,ON 1.627 vs σ_ON,OFF 3.264** (ratio 2.007) | the ON/OFF split |
| waves' **0.195 vs 0.000** on identical RNG | entropy + propagation rules |
| **lid suture worse than dark (−0.1458)** | Oja converging to the leading PC of whatever it is shown — **noise has no leading PC** |

**Everything PUT IN failed or was retracted:**

| number | put in | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| six `designed:1.0` kernels | Stage 1 | "biology emerged" **RETRACTED** |
| `w0 = 1.0` | `add_units` | a **431:1** DC prior; head start, not destination |
| `x_OFF = 1 − x_ON` | rung 6 | **degenerate BY CONSTRUCTION** |
| hand-placed thresholds | rung 5 | blind, `frac(w<0)=0.0000` for 51,200 steps |
| **`μ = 0.024`** | rung 8B, from GCAL's paper | θ wound to **26.9**, cell died, `rbar` = exactly 0 |

**The test, and it is sharp: is this number DETERMINED BY THE SYSTEM'S OWN CONSTRAINTS,
or CHOSEN TO MAKE AN OUTPUT LOOK RIGHT?** A number that falls out is fixed by something
real the system already has — its noise floor, its dynamic range, its own measured
statistics, a metabolic or information budget. A magic number is fixed by the answer you
wanted. **Both produce a float in the code. Only one survives a distribution shift**, and
that is exactly how rung 8B died: `μ` transferred fine within its own frame and vaporised
across two pathways whose drives differ ~6×.

**The corollary that makes this actionable — and it is the creator's "no view from
nowhere" thesis in numeric form:** *an absolute constant IS a view from nowhere.* It
asserts a scale the system has no way to know. **Rung 8B's finding — "an absolute setpoint
cannot transfer into unnormalised response units; GCAL's A requires GCAL's GC" — is a
special case of this rule.** Gain control is what makes the scale RELATIVE, and once the
scale is relative the setpoint stops being a magic number and becomes a fraction of a
dynamic range the system measures for itself. **This is also the log-weighted relative
admissibility grammar, arriving from the numeric side: ratios transfer, absolutes do
not.**

**Therefore, the fix for a failed constant is NEVER to tune it.** Tuning is §5's metric
surgery wearing a lab coat. **Ask instead: what would this number fall out of?** If the
answer is "nothing in the system — I would have to measure it against the answer", the
mechanism is incomplete and the constant is a symptom, not a knob. Import a paper's
MECHANISM, never its CONSTANTS — its constants fell out of ITS frame, which you do not
**⚠️ §13's ENGBERT EXEMPLAR NEEDS A THIRD CATEGORY — evidence in
`VISION_FAILURE_MODES_RESULTS.md`, for the supervisor to sequence (the eye rung's files are
not the failure-mode agent's to edit).** The defence below is right about the CONSTANT and
incomplete about the MECHANISM. **This seed's own comments say the crossover is
architecturally imposed:** `ey_saw_relax` — *"the relaxation is SLOW, and 3.2 is explicit
that **this is what makes the walk persistent**"*; `ey_saw_potential` — *"the long-lag
ANTIpersistence (**the half of Engbert's signature the potential is solely responsible
for**)"*. Each half of the signature is *solely* attributable to one imported architectural
component ⇒ **the model cannot NOT produce a crossover**, so α_s > 1 > α_l is a restatement
of its construction, not a prediction it risked. Independently corroborated by a review of
Engbert 2011's own construction, with no sight of this tree — **two readers, one cause.**
**The refinement:** *a mechanism whose ARCHITECTURE forces the signature you are measuring
is the same disease as an imported constant, wearing a mechanism's clothes — you did not
tune the number, and you did not risk it either.* **What STANDS: the MAGNITUDES** (1.1553 /
0.7590) are an untuned **calibration**, and their agreement with the published values is
real. **What does NOT: the qualitative signature**, which went in with the architecture.
Honest form: *"our implementation of Engbert's walk calibrates to Engbert's numbers"*, not
*"a crossover emerged from a self-avoiding walk"*. Retracts nothing; sharpens §13 exactly
where it planted its flag.

(Engbert's α is not a counter-example: we did not import 0.79, we built the walk and
**measured** 0.7590.)

**Applies to every future rung.** Before you commit a float, say in one sentence what it
falls out of. If you cannot, you have found a gap in the mechanism.

### §13.1 THE THIRD CATEGORY — architecture that FORCES the signature (2026-07-17, same day)

**§13's own exemplar was wrong, and the failure-mode agent caught it within the hour.**
I used Engbert's α as the type specimen of "fell out". The seed's **own comments** refute
me: `ey_saw_relax` — *"this is what makes the walk persistent"*; `ey_saw_potential` —
*"the ANTIpersistence (the half of Engbert's signature the potential is **solely
responsible for**)"*. Independently corroborated against Engbert 2011's construction by a
reviewer with no sight of the tree. **The model cannot NOT produce a crossover.** The
MAGNITUDES (1.1553 / 0.7590) are an untuned calibration and stand; the **QUALITATIVE
SIGNATURE went in with the architecture**.

**So there are THREE categories, not two:**

| category | example | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **fell out** of the mechanism | Weber–Fechner 0.9991 from a log receptor; centre-surround from a ZERO init; lid-suture-worse-than-dark from Oja's leading PC | **evidence** |
| **put in** as a CONSTANT | `μ=0.024`, `w0=1.0`, hand-placed thresholds | fails on distribution shift — **loudly** |
| **put in** as ARCHITECTURE | Engbert's crossover: two rules, each *solely responsible* for one half of the signature | **silently unfalsifiable** |

**A mechanism whose architecture FORCES the signature is the same disease as an imported
constant, wearing a mechanism's clothes** — and it is WORSE, because a bad constant dies
on a distribution shift while forced architecture reproduces the paper forever. It is the
`x_OFF = 1 − x_ON` disease (degenerate BY CONSTRUCTION) and the H3 disease (the two-phase
split wired into the node types, so the discriminating test **could not fail**) in a third
costume.

**The test: could this model have produced the OPPOSITE result?** If no rule could have
failed to yield the signature, reproducing it is not evidence — it is a tautology with
error bars. **Report which half of a signature each rule is solely responsible for.** If
the answer is "one rule per half", you have assembled the answer, not derived it.

### §13.2 "WORKS" AND "IS LOAD-BEARING" ARE DIFFERENT PROPERTIES (FM-0, 2026-07-17)

**The Engbert drift reproduces a published signature to two decimals and DRIVES NOTHING.**
Measured, not inferred: the manipulation is provably LIVE (`saw=1` walks 132 distinct
cells, path length 596; `saw=0` frozen at 0) and yet `D = max|saw1 − saw0|` is
**0.000000e+00 EXACTLY** on `lum`, `x`, `theta` AND `resp`, at every one of 400 steps.
Enumerated positively (never off a soft accessor): **0 of 23 eye rules read both a
GazeCell and an EyeCell; NO production admits a Gaze↔Eye edge — one is INADMISSIBLE, Γ
would reject it**; `present()` writes `frame[r,c]` and never calls `gaze_pos()`; and
**`gaze_pos()`'s only consumers in the whole tree are `walk()` and one test assertion —
the walk's sole consumer is the ruler that measures it.**

**A subsystem can be correct, published-accurate, gated, tested — and wired to nothing.**
Every §1 check passes, because §1 asks whether the MEASURE is sound, not whether the
mechanism REACHES anything.

**⇒ THE FIFTH CLAUSE OF §1: a mechanism must be shown to MOVE something downstream before
its statistics mean anything.** Run the vacuity gate FIRST, as FM-0 did: toggle the
mechanism and measure `max|on − off|` on every downstream attribute you claim it affects.
**`D == 0.0` exactly ⇒ the subsystem is decorative; STOP and burn no seed.** This is
cheaper than every experiment it saves.

**Corollary — the pattern the supervisor asserted is FALSIFIED, and the correction is more
useful.** I claimed *"the failure modes we can test map onto the parts that work; the ones
we cannot map onto the parts that do not."* **Wrong**: two of four modes map onto parts
that demonstrably WORK (the drift's α's; rung 7's emerged centre-surround) and are
untestable anyway, for two *different* structural reasons (an uncoupled subsystem; an
input alphabet of `{0,1}`). The clean pattern was an artifact of having only looked at the
broken parts. **The true statement: testable failure modes map onto the LOAD-BEARING
parts — a strictly smaller set, and the gap between "works" and "load-bearing" is exactly
where a ladder accumulates DECORATION.**

**This is why the creator's "can we replicate known failure modes? that is the real tell"
is the strongest instrument in this document.** A failure mode cannot be faked by
decoration, because **it is a claim about what the mechanism DRIVES**, not about what it
computes in isolation. FM-0 found in one afternoon what nine pre-registrations, an
adversarial review and a full gate suite did not.

## 12. A guard that runs the thing it guards is not a guard; a selector that matches by substring is not a selector

Two defects that produced **four different wrong baselines** in one session, both mine:

- **`test_vision_growth_migrated.py`'s corpus skip-guard called `preprocess_patches()`
  and only THEN tested emptiness** — but that function reshapes, and numpy cannot infer
  `-1` at size 0. `data/` is gitignored, so **every fresh worktree** got 5 ERRORS where
  it should have got 5 skips. Fixed: check `bsds_paths()` first; `preprocess_patches` is
  now total on empty input. **Guard before you touch, and make the guarded function
  total anyway.**
- **`pytest -k vision` matches `test_meaning_inference_migrated.py`** — because
  "pro**vision**al" contains "vision". Two non-vision failures have been reported as
  vision failures all session. **`-k` is a substring match, not a namespace.** Prefer an
  explicit file list or a marker.

**Consequence, and the reason this is a rule:** this session reported the vision baseline
as 122/0, 138/0, 145/10, 19 passed, 10/122, 156/0 and finally **153 vision passed / 0
failed** — for a suite with one answer. The supervisor relayed several as fact. Combined
with §10 (two binaries) and §11 (shared state), **every number needs its engine, its
commit, and its selector stated, or it is a rumour.**

**INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED, and that is worth recording.** The rung-7 agent, working in
a separate worktree with no sight of this section, hit **both** defects and diagnosed them
identically: `-k vision` collects `test_adoption.py`, `test_audio.py` and
`test_meaning_inference_migrated.py`'s `..._infers_provisional_sense_...` tests (36 files,
most unrelated), and the corpus guard crashes before it can fire because
`preprocess_patches` reshapes an empty array first. **Two agents, two worktrees, one
cause** — so these are properties of the bench, not of anyone's setup.

**THE CONCRETE SELECTOR (do this, don't just prefer it):**
`scripts/rung7_vision_bench.sh` — **16 explicitly named files**, no `-k`. At engine
`95167c01b7b3` it gives **163 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed**. A named selector is a file
you can diff; `-k` is a substring that silently changes meaning as tests are added.
**Name your selector, commit it, and quote its number with its engine.**

## §12.1 THE NINTH INERT INSTRUMENT WAS THE SUPERVISOR'S — AND IT WAS A `grep` (2026-07-17)

*Recorded because §12 is about selectors that lie, and this is the same defect one level
up: **counting tokens and inferring what they select.***

The two-eyes rung was briefed on this premise, twice, the second time with more
rhetorical confidence than the first (*"every `NodesOfType("Photoreceptor")` is a global
variable wearing graph clothes"*):

> *"The 23 eye rules contain 76 `NodesOfType` selections. That is a GLOBAL grab — a second
> eye would not be a second eye; both populations would dissolve into one soup."*

**It is FALSE.** It was produced by grepping `"type": "NodesOfType"` and inferring the
selected type without ever reading one. The audit, across **all 9 vision seeds**:

| | count |
|---|---|
| total `NodesOfType` selections | **185** |
| `*Params` (config) | 177 |
| `KernelGrowth` (also config: `eta`, `max_kernels`, …) | 8 |
| **genuine POPULATION grabs** | **0** |

**There is no `NodesOfType("Photoreceptor")` in this tree.** All 76 in `vision_eye.json`
are `EyeParams`. **Every rule in every vision seed — eye AND cortex — is already
hub-anchored** (`e -has_eyecell-> c`, `r -has_sunit-> u`, `r -has_cunit-> cu`). The eye
was never a singleton by rule scoping, and **two eyes already run**: distinct hubs,
disjoint cells, both waving, between-eye r = **−0.0077**, on unmodified code.

**The refactor that was briefed did not exist.** The rule this earns: **a claim about what
code SELECTS is not established by counting the tokens that select it.** Read one.

### §12.2 THE MEASURE THAT IS BLIND BY CONSTRUCTION — zero-lag on a travelling wave

The same rung nearly reported *"the waves carry no within-eye correlation, so Miller
1994's condition fails here"* — an **absence claim** — off a zero-lag Pearson r
(within-eye **−0.0441**, separation **−0.0635**). **A travelling wave reaches a cell and
its neighbour at DIFFERENT times, and refractoriness makes them mutually exclusive at any
instant: zero-lag reads ~0 for a PERFECT wave.** Smoothing over the window the learning
rule actually integrates:

| window | within-eye | between-eye | separation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (zero-lag) | −0.0441 | +0.0194 | **−0.0635** ← blind |
| 2 | +0.4377 | +0.0392 | +0.3985 |
| 8 | +0.7483 | +0.0675 | **+0.6808** |
| 32 | +0.8260 | +0.1423 | +0.6837 |

**The Miller condition HOLDS** (positive-controlled against a synthetic travelling wave,
which separates at every window). **Correlation is a statistic OF A TIMESCALE; quoting one
without its window is quoting a constant without its axis** (§1's "gated by its constants
but not the AXIS they parameterise", in the time domain).

### §12.3 `PickUnique` — the ambiguous config read is now LOUD (2026-07-17)

`Pick` is `iter().next()`: `Pick(NodesOfType("EyeParams"))` **silently returns one of N**
and the rest are inert. Measured: with two `WaveParams` nodes, `Pick` returns `default`
and the second node is ignored **without a word**. That is a silent wrong answer where
there should be an error — `.get('Name','')` and the guarded division (§1.1) in
selector form — and it is latent under **exactly** the mechanism monocular deprivation
depends on (a per-eye `eye_open`). **An MD arm is where a silently-inert config produces a
beautiful, publishable, entirely fake result**: deprive one eye, config ignored, ODI
shifts for some other reason, every §1 check passes.

and does not warn: **it reports perfect ocular dominance, from a key collision, and passes
every §1 check**, because the surviving eye really is the only input. `merge_bipolars()`
keys by eye and **asserts the count**. *Honest scope:* with the eye in the key a collision
is impossible, so that assert is **unreachable defensive code, not a gate that fires

### §10 rule 1b — THE PROVENANCE CHECK MUST RUN IN THE PROCESS THAT TAKES THE NUMBER

A green `tests/test_engine_provenance_migrated.py` certifies THE TREE'S CONFIGURATION UNDER
ITS OWN PREAMBLE. It does NOT certify that the process you are about to measure in loaded
the engine you think it did — **measured 2026-07-19: 7 PASSED in the same minute a plain
script in the same tree resolved `** WRONG ENGINE **`.** A bare `python -c` with
`sys.path.insert(0, '.')` picks up the canonical `.pth` first and the gate is silent about
it. **A GREEN GATE IN A DIFFERENT PROCESS IS NOT PROVENANCE.**

Now structural rather than remembered: `engine_preamble()` — the call rule 3 already
requires of every non-pytest entrypoint — computes the verdict from the module resident in
THIS process's `sys.modules` and RAISES `EngineProvenanceError` on `DIVERGED`, on an
unverifiable engine, and on stale Rust. **You cannot pin the engine without certifying what
you pinned.** 140 scripts covered with no edit to any of them. `conftest.py` passes
`strict=False` deliberately: under pytest the refusal would abort COLLECTION and move the
oracle's number (§9). **The gate reports; the preamble refuses; neither does the other's
job.** Write the record where the number is written: `rec["engine_provenance"] =
provenance_stamp()`.

### §10 rule 3b — A RUNTIME CHECK CANNOT SEE A PROCESS THAT NEVER RUNS IT

`domains/preamble_audit.py` is the independent static half — AST only, importing no engine,
**deliberately not computed by the machinery it checks.** It resolves the BINDING and looks
for a Call, so alias / qualified / dotted spellings are one case and a docstring is not a
call (the fifth substring-selector failure in this arc happened *inside the test written to
warn about substring selectors*). **Measured 2026-07-19: SEVEN vision measure scripts REPORT
provenance and never PIN.** `results/preamble_audit_floor.json` holds them as **LIVE
DEFECTS, NOT EXEMPTIONS.**

### §11 rec #4 (REPLACED) — THE MEASURED RECORD IS GENERATED, NOT WRITTEN

Rec #4 was a prose discipline for two rungs and was never applied, because **prose can only
be gated by a substring selector and this arc's record on those is 0–4.**
`results/seed_ledger_measured.json` is DERIVED from the AST scan and **gated for freshness**:
any seed added, moved or removed anywhere makes it red until `python3 -m domains.seed_record
--write`. The requirement attaches to the moment a rung's seeds LAND, not to the moment
someone writes a ledger row — which is the moment the old discipline reliably failed. **The
nuisance mode is a TRUE POSITIVE, and the diff it forces IS the record.** **A ledger row's
DECLARED block is a claim about the tree; this file is the tree.** *A clean record means
"nothing detected", never "nothing there".*

### §3 clause 8 — RECORD YOUR `check_claim` OUTPUT

A pre-registration must contain the verbatim verdict of `scripts/seed_claim.py <lo> <hi>` for
its block, **including the unresolved-sink count** — a claim that passes with unknown sinks
has verified nothing unless the silence is priced. §3.4 already demands "confirmatory seeds
never used for anything"; this makes that clause CHECKABLE rather than an honour system.
Enforced by `tests/test_instrument_seams_migrated.py` with a committed grandfather floor
(`results/prereg_claim_floor.json`, 95 documents) so it binds every rung AFTER it and none
before. **A MENTION IS NOT A RECORD:** "I ran check_claim and it was fine" does not satisfy
the gate; the pasted output does.

- **§2 CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT AND THE FIX WAS MECHANISM, NOT METRIC (same rung).** The
  setpoint's first estimator was the cell's existing EMA (`xbar`, β=0.991): a
  **tracking filter** whose variance never decays (L2 drift stuck at **0.078**), so
  it has **no stable fixed point** — precisely what §2 says cannot model
  development. A **cumulative mean** converges (drift **0.0021**) and is unbiased
  (0.146175 vs the input's 0.146197). **The lesson generalises: "it tracks the right
  value" and "it has a fixed point" are different properties** — the EMA tracked the
  mean correctly and was still disqualified.

- **Rung 6 — the SIGNED SIMPLE LAYER (ON/OFF split): the LAYER is BUILT; the
  DEVELOPMENT is NOT** (`VISION_RUNG6_PREREG.md`). No confirmatory arms were run
  (seeds 8000–8999 allocated, unused, clean) — the rung stopped at the
  CONVERGENCE gate.
  **RUNG 5'S BLOCKER IS REMOVED.** Every weight stays non-negative (Dale, gated)
  **yet the effective RF `w⁺ − w⁻` is signed** — what rung 5 measured as
  impossible (`frac(w<0)=0.0000`). Through the IDENTICAL frozen probe on which
  rung 5's units scored **OSI 0.004**, an ideal split cell scores **0.9115**.
  **THE RUNG'S MAIN FINDING, and it was not in the design: the THRESHOLD, not
  the split, is what makes the RESPONSE signed.** The split alone gives an ideal
  split-Gabor **OSI 0.0006** — the OFF channel's tonic drive (`Σw⁻ = 5.613`) sits
  above the signal (±2.3), so `act` never reaches 0, rectification never bites and
  F0 is flat (5.120 vs 5.055). Adding a spike threshold (`rate = max(act−θ,0)`,
  θ an EMA of the cell's own drive — the "iceberg", Priebe & Ferster 2008, placed
  on the ACTIVATION function as GCAL does, where it cannot flip `dw`'s sign) →
  **0.9115** on the same weights. **The split makes the FILTER signed; the
  THRESHOLD makes the RESPONSE signed.**

  RUNS AWAY (drift 0.004 → 0.461, clumpiness → 0.85, OSI decaying); at η=1e-4 it
  is stable but EMPTY (OSI 0.283 → 0.329 against an untrained **floor of 0.3168**,
  SESOI 0.0595) and the cells never become responsive (peak/base ~1.5 vs the
  ideal's 6.44). **Both of PROTOCOL §2's stop conditions at once.**
  **The mechanism is NOT a null instrument** — the positive control (a BIASED
  ensemble, one orientation) gives **OSI 0.878, peak/base 20.6, ON/OFF clumpiness
  0.718, and every cell prefers the orientation it was shown** — but that is
  measured INSIDE the transient, so it shows CAPABILITY, not a fixed point.
  **Diagnosis (ensemble degeneracy, per VISION_PRIOR_ART.md's correction — NOT
  "the average has no direction"):** the same rule at the same η scores 0.878
  biased and 0.32 on waves. Structurally, **the complementary split `x_OFF = 1−x`
  is itself degenerate** — it determines the OFF channel exactly, so
  `C_ON,OFF(d) = −C_ON,ON(d)` identically and the two channels carry **no
  independent correlation structure**. Miller 1994 gets segregation precisely from
  ON/OFF correlation functions with DIFFERENT spatial dependence (centre-surround
  RFs of different sizes). **The ON/OFF sign is NECESSARY (it removes rung 5's
  blocker) but NOT SUFFICIENT (it adds no structure for waves to sculpt).**
  **Named next:** give the channels independent correlation structure via retinal
  lateral inhibition **as a RULE** over the existing `neighbour` edges (a
  hand-built DoG — `substrate_rs/vision.py::lgn_pair` — is the bolt-on error and
  is rejected); lateral interactions between SUnits (rung 4's `vm_burst_lateral`
  is the precedent); a stability regime for the subtractive rule (a mechanism, not
  a search between 1e-4 and 5e-4).
  **The freeze bug is FIXED and GATED** (`OnOffParams.frozen` gates every learning
  rule INCLUDING the threshold's adaptation — adaptation is plasticity): real
  freeze max |dw| **0.000e+00**, defective (`oja=0`) **2.281e-02**. It changes **no
  committed result** — rungs 1/2/4 read WEIGHTS with no stimulus presented, so no
  rule fires during their read-out.

### ADVANCED LIGHTING L4 — SHADOW vs REFLECTANCE EDGES (2026-07-19)

- **BUILT:** edge ATTRIBUTION. An ILLUMINANT edge scales every channel by ONE
  factor and so PRESERVES chromatic ratios; a REFLECTANCE edge changes them.
  The predicate is **L2's own `_slowvar_clause` with the quantifier moved from
  SPACE to WAVELENGTH** — same cross-multiplication, same two-roundings
  envelope, index pair (locale,locale) → (channel,channel). **NO new Rust, NO
  new constant.**
- **THE CROSSING:** shown RAW luminance, the UNMODIFIED `vision_border_ownership`
  seed mints **2** proto-objects — the material patch **and the cast shadow**.
  Shown the field L4 decided (`l4_flood`, `bo_label`'s min-flood with
  `Eq(val,val)` replaced by the ratio predicate), it mints **1**: the patch.
  **A shadow boundary is no longer an object boundary; a material boundary still
  is.** L2 recovered identities on both sides of a shadow edge *without knowing
  an edge was there*; that gap is now closed.
- **L4 SITS BESIDE L2/L3, NOT ON TOP.** It uses no reference frame, no
  `compares_to`, no codebook, no locale pairing, no registration, no anchor —
  **strictly weaker assumptions.** Consequently **L3's "anchor of the anchor" is
  untouched**, and **L4 does not recover reflectance**: no L2/L3 arm consumes an
  L4 attribute. Wiring attribution back into constancy is the named next rung.
- **THREE NEGATIVES, ALL PREDICTED IN ADVANCE, ONE MECHANISM:** a **CHROMATIC**
  shadow is misclassified 6/6 (blue skylight vs yellow sun — **the physically
  common case, NOT solved**); **PROPORTIONAL** materials are misread 2/2
  (irreducible to any local ratio cue); and the **noise floor FAILS its
  pre-registered exact-0 at 2/1200**, both leaks being near-proportional random
  triples — **the floor's residual IS the proportional ambiguity, arising by
  chance.**
- **§1.1 FOR THE FIFTH TIME, AND IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** The two injected defects
  are exact opposites and **each passes the other's floor**: under
  everything-is-a-shadow all 36 headline arm-A tests stay GREEN; under
  refuse-everything arm B, all 6 chromatic tests, and a **perfect 0/1200 noise
  floor** stay GREEN. **The arms that caught BOTH are the NOT-AN-OBJECT-BOUNDARY
  arm and the DISAGREEMENT arm.** Neither floor alone is a gate.
- **§13.1 SELF-DECLARED:** the headline shadow arm is **ENTAILED by the
  derivation** (the envelope is a proven upper bound under the neutral

- **THE AUDIT IS THE PAYLOAD.** Six candidate certifiers for the pooled scene
